judged_text: handleCancelBooking falls back to prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) with no check that the credential belongs to bookingToDelete.user or any booking participant, whereas the old code only used credentials found in bookingToDelete.user.credentials and silently skipped foreign ids. A booking reference carrying a foreign credentialId now resolves to that credential and its OAuth key is used to delete events in the foreign calendar on cancellation, turning previously inert stored reference data into cross-user calendar deletion.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking`, when a booking calendar reference has `credentialId` but it is not found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, the new code falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then uses that credential to instantiate a calendar and call `deleteEvent(...)` (see the added `foundCalendarCredential` lookup and subsequent `getCalendar(calendarCredential)` + `calendar?.deleteEvent(uid, evt, externalCalendarId)`). There is no verification that the fetched credential belongs to `bookingToDelete.user` (e.g., matching `userId`/`teamId`) or otherwise is authorized for this booking. Previously, the logic only used credentials present in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and would effectively skip unknown/foreign ids. This change can turn a stored reference containing a foreign `credentialId` into an action performed with that foreign credential, enabling cross-user calendar deletion if such a reference exists.
